- Production target: inference for triage assistant, 200 concurrent sessions, median p99 latency target ~120ms

Hi Daniel — thanks for the clear constraints.

High-level suggestion: we should run a 6-week MAP that ties evaluation milestones to procurement checkpoints so you can decide on reserve vs private before the 60-day window closes. Draft outline below (I'll attach a formal MAP spreadsheet after our OK):

Week 0 (kickoff): mutual scoping call, collect sample prompts/payloads, confirm data handling and KMS requirements.
Week 1–2 (eval staging): deploy a short-lived private tenant or Dedicated eval instances; run synthetic load tests and pilot traffic with a subset of users.
Week 3 (qual checks): run acceptance tests (functional accuracy, latency SLOs, throughput at target concurrency, KV-prefetch cache effectiveness).
Week 4 (security/compliance): deliver SOC2 snapshot, audit logs walkthrough, and KMS integration demo.
Week 5 (procurement-ready): finalize sizing, pricing estimate, and contract terms for reservation or Private license.
Week 6 (close/onboarding): sign and schedule reserved capacity or private install; plan canary rollout and rollback policy.

Initial sizing options we should consider (very approximate until we have real traces):
- Dedicated reserved (single pool): 8 x A100-80GB equivalent to sustain 200 concurrent sessions with batching and KV caching, expected P99 ~110–140ms depending on prompts.
- Private on-prem (customer-provided infra): 12 x A40/RTX-class nodes with sharded model serving to hit throughput and redundancy goals; longer lead time for on-prem setup and acceptance testing.

I'll loop Marcus for a quick technical sizing doc and a .csv with per-variant estimates. Can you confirm the 60-day procurement cutoff and who will own acceptance tests on your side?

Thanks — attaching the initial MAP template and the SOC2 snapshot we can share for your procurement review.

Best,
Ava Chen
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: SigmaHealth capacity MAP & evaluation timeline (Dedicated vs Private lead times)

Looping in a more technical sizing breakdown and notes. See attached CSV stub (capacity-estimates.csv) — numbers are conservative and assume medium-length prompts (avg 150 tokens in / 400 tokens out), with batching and KV caching enabled.

Notes:
- Dedicated (hosted, reserved pool) lead time: provisioning a reserved GPU pool can be done within 2–3 weeks for US regions if we have capacity; procurement needs to finalize commitment/term for reservation.
- Private (VPC/on-prem) lead time: VPC private deployment (managed by Redwood in your VPC) about 3–4 weeks for network config + KMS integration; full on-prem appliance (air-gapped) is 6–10 weeks depending on customer infra readiness and access.
- Sizing guidance: 200 concurrent sessions target -> estimate 6–10 GPUs for low-latency conservative config, 10–14 GPUs for high availability + headroom. The A100-80GB family provides better single-model latency; quantized LLM variants can drop required GPUs by ~30% but require quality validation.
- Acceptance tests:
  1) Latency: p50/p95/p99 under target concurrency (p99 <= 150ms for critical paths)
  2) Throughput: sustain X tokens/sec for 30m window without queue growth
  3) Quality sanity: prompt-set with baseline BLEU/ROUGE/embedding similarity checks or human spot checks
  4) Security: KMS encryption in transit and at rest verified, access audit events present for a week-long sample

Risks:
- If procurement cannot commit to a reservation, capacity guarantees are limited during peak industry demand months (June–Aug).
- On-prem installs often hit delays due to networking/firewall and hardware procurement.

I'll keep the CSV updated with delta scenarios; happy to review with your infra and procurement leads.

—Marcus
Staff SRE, Redwood Inference

Attachments: capacity-estimates.csv
